title: Ex-Cale88 co-owner, BOC official to testify in Sara Duterte impeachment trial
summary: Dr. Lourdes Tingson-Lebosada, who is also the Vice President's dentist, is expected to testify on Cale88's organizational structure, government registrations, business operations, ownership, and…

blocks.text: VEEP. Vice President Sara Duterte talks to supporters as she prepares to leave the Quezon City Regional Trial Court after the postponement of the arraignment for her grave threats case, on October 9, 2026.

Dr. Lourdes Tingson-Lebosada, who is also the Vice President's dentist, is expected to testify on Cale88's organizational structure, government registrations, business operations, ownership, and financial affairs

MANILA, Philippines – A former co-owner of Cale88 Foods Corporation, who is also Vice President Sara Duterte‘s dentist, is expected to testify before the Senate impeachment court when her trial resumes on December 1.

The defense counsel submitted a manifestation dated November 25 asking the Senate impeachment court to issue subpoenas ad testificandum et duces tecum to Dr. Lourdes Tingson-Lebosada and direct her to participate during the proceedings scheduled from December 1 to 4.
Lebosada was also directed to bring certified true copies of the following documents:

items: Registration documents of Cale88 Foods Corporation, including relevant government records;
Documents relating to the company’s finances and business transactions; and
Other documents relevant to the foregoing.

blocks.text: Cale88, a banana chips production company co-owned by Lebosada and Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio, came under scrutiny during the impeachment trial after Anti-Money Laundering Council records showed that it received P776 million in cash inflows despite having only P125,000 in paid-up capital and declaring P208 million in sales.

Lawyer Alex Cabrera, who prepared a forensic financial report on Duterte’s bank and financial records, described Cale88’s business model as “implausible” and likened its operations to a “revolving door,” which he said was indicative of money laundering.
Lebosada is expected to testify on Cale88’s organizational structure, government registrations, business operations, ownership, and financial affairs.

The defense also sought a subpoena for Agaton Teodoro Uvero, deputy commissioner of the Assessment and Operations Coordinating Group of the Bureau of Customs. Uvero is expected to testify on Cale88’s exportation records under the custody of the BOC.
The impeachment court confirmed the issuance of subpoenas to both witnesses.

“As of this morning, Thursday, November 26, 2026, the Office of the Clerk of Court has completed service of both subpoenas — serving the Office of Bureau of Customs Deputy Commissioner Atty. Agaton Teodoro O. Uvero personally at 9:05 am, and serving Dr. Lourdes Tingson-Lebosada in Davao City via electronic mail at 9:54 am pursuant to the Court’s electronic service directive,” said impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol.
The impeachment trial is currently on hold to give way to Senate plenary deliberations on the proposed P7.2-trillion national budget. Proceedings are scheduled to resume on December 1. – Rappler.com
